titulo: Fridge part 2: should you cover leftovers? And how many days do they last?
fuentes: USDA FSIS — Leftovers and Food Safety: https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety (leftovers 3 to 4 days in the fridge, 3 to 4 months in the freezer; refrigerate within 2 hours, 1 hour above 90 °F)
USDA FSIS — Cold Food Storage Chart: soups and stews 2 to 3 months in the freezer (quality)

frases.texto: In part one, I told you not to let leftovers cool on the counter.
frases.estilo: Friendly, picking up where we left off.

frases.texto: Next question: should you cover them?
Yes. The USDA says covering keeps moisture in and other fridge smells out.
But what matters more is how many days they last.
That chili has an expiration date.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The USDA says three to four days in the fridge.
Won't finish it? Freeze it. For soups and stews, the USDA says quality holds two to three months.
Heads up: that only counts if it's in the fridge within two hours, or one hour if it's over ninety degrees out.
Today, stick a date label on every container.
Send this to the friend who stores the whole pot with the lid on.
